title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity, from China's rapid launch cadence to new funding rounds aimed at enhancing satellite operations. Meanwhile, the U.S. is doubling down on space resilience as budget allocations increase, signaling a strategic pivot in defense priorities.

themes.title: China's Launch Spree Stalls
themes.body: China's recent flurry of four launches in three days raises eyebrows, especially with the silence following the Kuaizhou–11 launch. This could indicate either a strategic pause or a deeper issue within their launch cadence.

themes.title: Funding Flows into Space Tech
themes.body: Dawn Aerospace's $25 million raise and True Anomaly's $190 million Series C highlight the growing investor appetite for space technology. As the industry matures, expect more capital to chase innovative solutions, particularly in satellite operations.

themes.title: U.S. Defense Budget Boosts Space
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion increase for space resilience underscores a serious commitment to bolstering U.S. capabilities in orbit. This funding will likely fuel initiatives aimed at countering emerging threats in the space domain.

themes.title: Collision Avoidance Takes Center Stage
themes.body: The partnership between Look Up and Skynopy for an automated satellite collision avoidance service reflects the urgent need for improved space traffic management. As more satellites populate the skies, the risk of collisions becomes a pressing concern for operators.
